$comment: D-TARGET-ARM64-W-CONSTRAINT-BINDS-A-CLASS-NO-C-VALUE-EVER-LIVES-IN · D-LIR-SUBREGISTER-AWARE-ALLOCATION-FOR-ALIASED-VIEWS. ★★★ THIS EXAMPLE'S aarch64 ARMS WERE BORN RED AND COULD NOT COMPILE AT ALL: every `"w"`-bound floating operand was refused at debug AND release with *input 0 (constraint "w") binds register class 'vr', but the value it carries lives in class 'fpr'*, about programs `aarch64-linux-gnu-gcc 13.3.0 -O2` compiles (allocating `d0`). One working reference makes the behaviour REQUIRED. The x86-64 arms are the CONTROL: `"x"` ⇒ `fpr` has always had exactly the shape R1 gives aarch64 — one class whose members are the FULL 16-byte registers holding 8-byte doubles — and has always compiled, which is what separates *the aarch64 config was wrong* from *this pipeline cannot express the construct*. ★★★ WHY THE EXIT CODE IS A RESULT AND NOT A STRUCTURE PIN: the failure mode this replaces is a LOUD refusal, so a compile-only arm would pass the moment the constraint bound to anything at all — including a GPR, which is what the pipeline did before the class-blind asm move was fixed (a live silent miscompile: `"w"(double)` copying `x_` for a value living in `d_`). Only EXECUTION distinguishes *the operand reached a floating-point register* from *the operand reached a register*. Each shape carries its own exit code so a failure names which one broke. ★★ SHAPE 4 IS THE ONE THAT NEEDED THE FREE LIST RATHER THAN THE BINDING: before R1 the `vr` free list was empty BY CONSTRUCTION (the AAPCS64 convention named only the d-views, so `buildFreeLists` produced no VR registers and every VR value spilled — `R_SpilledDueToPressure` at release, `exhausted the per-class scratch pool` at debug). Eight simultaneously-live constrained operands is more than any scratch pool, so shape 4 passes only if they were genuinely ALLOCATED. ⚠ THE `volatile` SEEDS ARE LOAD-BEARING: without them the release pipeline folds every value before lowering and the file would pass without binding an operand to a floating-point register at all. ⚠ THIS SENTENCE SAID THE TEMPLATES SAY `nop` BECAUSE THE aarch64 gas DIALECT SPELLS NO FP MNEMONIC — ✔MEASURED true when written (`asm-arm64-gas.lang.json` declared 51 instructions, not one floating; the aarch64 twin of the gap `c_inline_asm_x86_sse_operands` records for x86-64) and it EXPIRED in P54, which declared seven floating mnemonics (`fadd fsub fmul fdiv fneg fcmp fmov`) under D-ASM-DIALECTS-DECLARE-A-REGISTER-CLASS-NO-INSTRUCTION-CAN-NAME; `c_inline_asm_arm64_fp_operands` now executes them. ★ THE `nop` TEMPLATES STAY, for a BETTER reason than the one that expired: this example's subject is that the CONSTRAINT binds and allocates, and a `nop` cannot pass by accident through an instruction that would have moved the value anyway.
